question.leadin: This leader was assassinated by Nathuram Godse [God-say] in 1948.
question.text: Name this central figure of India's independence movement who was given the honorific "Mahatma," or "Great Soul."
question.clue: With Lord Irwin, this person ended the salt tax in exchange for ending the Salt March.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Din-i Ilahi.
swap.text: The Din-i Ilahi was a new syncretic religion promulgated by Akbar, the ruler of this empire. This Muslim empire ruled over most of India under its last major emperor, Aurangzeb.
swap.clue: The "Nine Jewels" were employed by a monarch of this empire who abolished a tax on non-Muslims.

question.text: A notable example of Mughul architecture is this white-domed mausoleum in Agra, built by Akbar's grandson Shah Jahan for his wife.
question.clue: A tree-lined reflecting pool is in front of this structure surrounded by four minarets.

swap.text: After he murdered Mahatma Gandhi, Godse was put on trial in the Red Fort of this Indian city. A "New" district of this city is the capital of India.
swap.clue: Plans for George VI to impress the "native minds" of this city by traveling to it via plane to hold a grand ceremony at Coronation Park were dropped because of their lack of political or financial tact.

question.leadin: She oversaw her country's first nuclear test, Operation Smiling Buddha.
question.text: Identify this only female prime minister of India, who was assassinated by two of her Sikh bodyguards after ordering a raid on the Golden Temple at Amritsar. Her son Rajiv took office after she was assassinated.
question.clue: This politician's government carried out forced sterilizations during a period of restricted civil liberties called the Emergency.

swap.leadin: This Seven Years' War battle helped destroy French influence in India.
swap.text: Name this battle which saw British forces supporting the Bengalese pretender Mir Jafar rout Nawab Siraj-ud-daula's army despite being outnumbered seventeen to one.
swap.clue: It took place a year after the death of the beloved Alivardi Khan, whose nephew was killed by the son of the perfidious Mir Jafar following it.

question.text: The Kingdom of Kandy was located on this island, separated from India by the Palk strait. It was later known as Ceylon during the colonial period.
question.clue: The Portuguese presence in this modern-day country was eliminated by a Dutch-allied kingdom known as Kandy.

swap.text: This ruler hid with his son in baskets designated for sweets to escape the clutches of Aurangzeb. More famously, he ripped open the stomach of Afhal Khan after he tried to murder him. This man is known for establishing the Maratha Empire.
swap.clue: That general, Afzal Khan, was the subordinate of Sultan Ali Adil Shah of the Bijapur region, where this man engaged in guerrilla warfare.

question.text: The prince Sri Lumay was half-Malay and half-[this ethnicity]. The three great kingdoms to rule these Dravidian peoples were the Chola, Chera, and Pandyas.
question.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

swap.text: In Khara, up to 150 Maoist rebels were killed in a failed attack on an army camp. In May 2002, Prime Minister Deuba dissolved parliament and was summarily expelled from the ruling party, leading King Gyendera to reimpose emergency rule. For 15 points-name this Asian country in which insurrections have escalated since the royal family was killed by a crown prince in 2001.
swap.clue: Chhetris dominated this kingdom's politics, especially after the Kot Massacre reduced its king to a figurehead.

question.leadin: This man was barred from receiving a visa to visit the United States after the 2002 riots in Gujarat, the state where this man served as Chief Minister for over ten years.
question.text: Name this member of the BJP who won a national election in May of 2014.
question.clue: This Indian prime minister, the successor of Manmohan Singh, issued the decree.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Five Great Mountains in China known as the Wu Yue.
swap.text: None of the Five Great Mountains are located in this mountain range located at the border of Tibet and China that contains K2 and Mt. Everest.
swap.clue: The McMahon Line and Line of Actual Control run through this mountain range.

question.text: The day after the mosque's invasion, protesters burned down this city's U.S. embassy. It replaced Karachi as Pakistan's capital in 1961.
question.clue: Built in 1960, name this city that became the capital of a South Asian nation that split from India in 1947.

swap.leadin: Kenya's oldest print newspaper was founded by an immigrant from this colony.
swap.text: Give this colony. Immigrants from this colony formed an ambulance corps that helped save lives at the Battle of Spion Kop during the Boer War.
swap.clue: Lord Curzon established this colony's North-West Frontier Province, whose western border was set at the Durand Line to settle the Great Game with Russia.

question.text: The Wadiyar Dynasty ruled this successor state to Vijayanagara. Hayder Ali and Tipu Sultan, who seized power in this kingdom, deployed rockets that would later inspire William Congreve in three namesake wars against the British.
question.clue: Forces of this kingdom deployed iron-cased rockets with attached blades to great effect at the Battle of Pollilur.

swap.leadin: Members of this clan include the general Prithvaraj of the Chauhan dynasty, who won the Battle of Tarain against Mohammed of Ghor.
swap.text: Identify this people whose princess Harka Bai became Mariam-uz-Zamani after a matrimonial alliance in 1562.
swap.clue: An entire ruling family of these people called the Guhilas was wiped out in 1303 after the capture of the Chittor Fort.

question.leadin: This empire's power was broken after its forces, convinced that a British cavalry escort for an ammunition resupply was a flanking maneuver, retreated at the Battle of Ferozeshah (feh-roh-zay-shah).
question.text: Name this major power in the Punjab in the early 19th century, which clashed with forces of the British East India Company in two namesake wars in the 1840s. This highly militaristic empire was founded by Ranjit.
question.clue: Victories at the battles of Attock and Jamrud, among others, brought this empire to its westernmost extent at the expense of the Durrani Empire.

swap.leadin: This man dispatched the Younghusband expedition to Lhasa to establish a British presence in Tibet before the Russians could get there.
swap.text: Identify this successor of Lord Elgin as Viceroy of India.
swap.answerHtml: Lord Curzon [or George Nathaniel Curzon, Marquees Curzon or Baron Curzon of Kedleston or Earl Curzon of Kedleston]

question.leadin: Enforced by the Viceroy Chelmsford, this legislation gave his government special "emergency powers" to censor the press, detain without trial, and arrest suspects without warrant. FTPE.
question.text: Also known as the "Black Acts," name this 1919 legislation which was passed over the unanimous opposition of the Indian members of the Supreme Legislative Council.
question.clue: The Amritsar protestors were expressing opposition to these laws, which addressed Indian sedition by removing the rights of warrant, habeas corpus, and appeal from those subject to the British Raj.

swap.text: This woman, the subject of a 520-episode docudrama on Zee TV, was a widow of Gangadhar Rao who particularly hated the Doctrine of Lapse. She rounded up an army to reclaim her annexed kingdom during the 1857 Rebellion and led a big fight, but was defeated by the Central India Force led by Hugh Rose.
swap.clue: Among the rulers of the princely states active after the fall of Maratha was this queen who died fighting the British at Gwalior Fort. Subhas Chandra Bose named his all-women regiment of the Indian National Army for this queen.
